company: Alipay launched in 2004 to help create trust between online buyers and sellers. Its parent company was formed in October 2014 as Ant Financial Services Group and was renamed Ant Group in July 2020. Ant expanded from payments into consumer and merchant finance, wealth and insurance distribution, and technology services.

Chinese authorities suspended Ant's dual-market IPO days before its planned November 2020 debut. The pre-pricing target was about $280 billion; the planned offering was reported at more than $310 billion at pricing. In July 2023, a proposed buyback implied $78.5 billion. That is the latest disclosed valuation marker identified here, not a current market price: Ant has not announced a more recent priced round or confirmed current valuation.

Alibaba accounts for its share of Ant's results one quarter in arrears, so reported profit figures require period labels. Reuters calculated RMB4.7 billion of profit for Ant's three months ended June 30, 2026, reported on August 20, 2026, up 1% year over year. This follows RMB4.74 billion for the three months ended March 31, 2025, reported in August 2025, which Reuters said was down 60.5% year over year.

Ant reported RMB35.03 billion of R&D investment in 2025, including AI-related work, after RMB23.45 billion in 2024. The 2024 amount is confirmed by Ant's 2024 Sustainability Report; the company said it was up 10.7% year over year.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Ant remains a useful case study in how fintech scale, regulation, and technology investment interact in China. Its payments network and financial-services distribution matter to the economics of consumer credit and platform businesses, while the separation of Ant International, Ant Digital Technologies, and OceanBase creates distinct capital-raising and possible-listing paths that should not be conflated with an Ant Group IPO.

changed.text: Ant completed a $14B private financing, then the largest venture-style round on record.
Ant’s planned $34.5B dual listing, which implied a valuation above $300B, was suspended days before trading.
The company undertook a regulator-driven restructuring of its consumer-finance and governance arrangements.
Bright Smart Securities said Ant Group became its indirect controlling shareholder after the acquisition completed on March 30, 2026; its June results said Ant indirectly owned 50.63%.

Reported developments at independent units included Ant International's planned $1B private round at a reported $10B-plus pre-money valuation and possible Hong Kong listing, an Ant Digital Technologies pre-IPO round, and OceanBase's reported plan to seek up to RMB3B. Ant International later said it had raised $1.2B. Except for the announced $1.2B raise, these plans and terms were not confirmed by the companies.
Reuters calculated RMB4.7B of Ant profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 from Alibaba's earnings disclosure, up 1% year over year.

takeaways: Alipay's payments network remains Ant's central distribution asset.
The $78.5B figure is a July 2023 buyback marker, not a current market valuation; no later Ant Group priced financing is confirmed here.
The latest reported profit calculation is RMB4.7B for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, reported August 20, 2026; it should not be relabelled as a later quarter.
Ant International, Ant Digital Technologies, and OceanBase have separate reported capital-market activity. Reported plans are not confirmed IPOs or valuations until officially disclosed.
